title: A clear boundary ends an old version

captions.physics: Noticing what a familiar picture invents
captions.energy: Finding stable foundations for shared explanation

meaning: Your shared view can recognise an earlier version’s ending when a familiar picture’s incompleteness gains an understandable boundary.
text: Finding that a familiar explanation no longer holds can feel sad. Death in the emotional position of Ajna experiences an exhausted view ending. The Moon in the physical position helps notice what the familiar picture supplied for itself. The Emperor in energy supports seeking stable foundations. Together these roles let you name the earlier version’s boundary while preserving footing for further understanding, rather than needing an immediate replacement that promises everything.

For example, you examine an old packing list for trips. You thought it covered any weather. Now you notice that some conditions are never named: a general feeling of preparedness supplied them. **A clear boundary lets an earlier version end without losing footing.** The list remains useful for stated conditions while its universal image ends. Losing a simple completed picture may bring regret. Your shared view gains a more dependable structure: what the list actually covers is visible, alongside a separate question that still needs foundations of its own.

The risk is treating the end of a universal version as the list becoming entirely useless. Actual content disappears too. Wanting stable foundations helps separate these conclusions. A promise to cover everything ends while named conditions retain significance. Understanding stays coherent when it bears the loss of former simplicity and rests on a clear boundary instead of immediately seeking another equally comprehensive answer.
